document_title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
short_description: NIST's final transition plan (October 2026) for moving from quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms to post-quantum standards. Every quantum-vulnerable signature and key-establishment parameter set in NIST standards (RSA, ECDSA and finite-field or elliptic-curve DH and MQV at 112 bits of classical security or more; EdDSA at 128 bits or more) is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035. ML-KEM-768 is the recommended default ML-KEM parameter set, HQC becomes approved once its FIPS is published, and a hybrid key-establishment scheme can be FIPS 140-validated when at least one input comes from an approved scheme. It supports Executive Order 14412 and OMB M-26-15, which set earlier federal deadlines for the most sensitive systems: post-quantum key establishment by 31 December 2030 and signatures by 31 December 2031.
